question: Is a good name a blessing or curse?
summary: The wisdom tradition treats a good reputation as one of life's highest goods. Ecclesiastes 7:1 ranks a good name above precious ointment and Proverbs 22:1 ranks it above great riches. Luke 6:26 flips the valuation — Jesus pronounces a woe on those of whom all speak well, on the grounds that the same kind of universal approval was given to the false prophets. The shared term is reputation, but the Hebrew sages prize it and the Lukan Jesus treats it as a danger sign.

reconcile.connective: Gill limits Jesus's woe to praise purchased by compromise, distinguishing it from the good name Ecclesiastes and Proverbs praise.

discrepancy.connective: Daniel G. Taylor's BibViz Project (citing EvilBible.com) presses the point: Ecclesiastes and Proverbs praise a good name while Luke 6:26 curses universal praise.

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill directly reconciles the woe with the wisdom tradition's praise of a good name by limiting Luke 6:26's target to praise won from bad men, explicitly excepting the good word of good men as no bad sign.
excerpts.source_note_text:
Woe unto you when all men shall speak well of you!.... The word "all", is left out in the Vulgate Latin, Syriac, Arabic; Persic: and Ethiopic versions, and is wanting in many copies, though it is in the Alexandrian copy; and the meaning is, it looks ill in persons, when the men of the world, wicked men, all of them, or the greater part of them, applaud and commend them; for this can never be, if they are truly religious persons, and are faithful to their principles, and upright in their practices; and do not connive at, or comply with the errors and evil ways of wicked men; for it is no bad sign, to have the good word of good men, and therefore these must be excepted, and the passage must be limited to bad men;
for so did their fathers to the false prophets; they spoke well of them, and heaped favours, riches, and honours upon them, that they might prophesy unto them things; Kg1 22:6, smooth things and deceit.
